description.value: The study examined how emotional context and emotional valence influence approach and avoidance behavior and associated amygdala and striatal BOLD activity during an emotional go/nogo task.

spans.text: The objective of this study was to examine the influence of emotional information in biasing performance during a go/nogo task and the biological basis underlying this influence.

value: we predicted that subjects would respond more slowly when pressing to (approaching) fearful faces relative to happy or neutral faces
we predicted that subjects would have more difficulty withholding responses to (avoiding) nogo (nontarget) faces with happy expressions
we predicted that successfully inhibiting responses to happy nontargets would be associated with increased BOLD signal in frontostriatal regions involved in inhibitory control
we hypothesized that increased amygdala activation would interfere with cortical functions and be associated with impaired task performance in terms of reaction time to negative expressions
